entities.name: GraphRAG
entities.description: A pipeline that uses prompts for initialization to extract knowledge.

entities.name: GPT-4
entities.description: A large language model used for entity and relationship extraction.
entities.evidence: prompts, designed for GPT-4, are used in the default GraphRAG initialization pipeline

entities.name: HotPotQA
entities.description: A sample dataset used to evaluate entity extraction performance.
entities.evidence: in a sample dataset (HotPotQA, Yang et al., 2018)

entities.name: Self-Reflection
entities.description: A prompt engineering technique where an LLM evaluates its own output to improve it.
entities.evidence: Self-reflection is a prompt engineering technique where the LLM generates an answer, and is then prompted to evaluate its output for correctness, clarity, or completeness

entities.name: gpt-4-turbo
entities.description: The specific model version used in the entity extraction prompt evaluation.
entities.evidence: generic entity extraction prompt with gpt-4-turbo

entities.name: Chunk Size
entities.description: The size of text segments processed by the LLM, affecting extraction cost and quantity.
entities.evidence: Using larger chunk size is less costly in terms of calls to the LLM

entities.name: Entity References
entities.description: The count of entities detected during extraction, varying with chunk size and iterations.

entities.name: Logit Bias
entities.description: A parameter used to force the LLM to make a yes/no decision during assessment.
entities.evidence: using a logit bias of 100 to force a yes/no decision

relationships.description: The GraphRAG initialization pipeline uses prompts designed for GPT-4.
relationships.evidence: The following prompts, designed for GPT-4, are used in the default GraphRAG initialization pipeline

relationships.description: GPT-4 extracts entity references from the HotPotQA dataset.
relationships.evidence: in a sample dataset (HotPotQA, Yang et al., 2018), GPT-4 extracted almost twice as many entity references

relationships.description: Larger chunk sizes are less costly but tend to result in fewer extracted entity references.
relationships.evidence: Using larger chunk size is less costly in terms of calls to the LLM. However, the LLM tends to extract few entities from chunks of larger size

relationships.description: Self-reflection allows the use of larger chunk sizes without a drop in quality.
relationships.evidence: This approach allows us to use larger chunk sizes without a drop in quality

relationships.description: Logit bias is a component of the self-reflection process used to force binary decisions.
relationships.evidence: using a logit bias of 100 to force a yes/no decision

relationships.description: The number of entity references detected varies based on the number of self-reflection iterations performed.
relationships.evidence: Entity references detected varies with chunk size and self-reflection iterations
